reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a named trading platform by directing viewers to register, activate an app, invest money, and expect stated daily profits tied to investment amounts. It also describes referral-based income and rank rewards linked to other participants, referral activity, and team-business thresholds. The slides reinforce investment, daily-bonus, and large reward claims, although the available video evidence does not establish whether payments, losses, platform operation, or advertised returns actually occurred.

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation does not describe returns as risk-free: it says, "You will earn and lose by trading with the same method." It also discloses a minimum withdrawal and a 15% withdrawal charge. Those qualifications matter when assessing whether the speaker is concealing downside. The profit claims deserve scrutiny, but the record does not establish that any viewer received the stated returns, or that the stated trading activity did not occur.

citations.quote: You will earn and lose by trading with the same method.
MINIMUM WITHDRAWAL OR P TO P TRANSFER, $10 MINIMUM WITHDRAWAL CHARGES 15%

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies confident profit language and referral levels, but those quotes do not erase the express possibility of losses or the disclosed withdrawal charge. Nor does a contact invitation establish that money was taken or a return was falsely reported. The question is whether the available presentation establishes deception, not whether its claims warrant caution.

citations.quote: You will earn and lose by trading with the same method.
MINIMUM WITHDRAWAL CHARGES 15%

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A brief acknowledgment of possible losses does not change the dominant invitation: viewers are told to select and activate an investment package and then expect continuing profits. The presentation supplies daily return figures tied to invested amounts. Disclosing a withdrawal charge does not substantiate the trading or the advertised returns.

If you invest from 50$ to 1,000$ you will get a 0.25% to 0.75% daily bonus

opening.argument: Judge, much of this presentation walks through how a proposed platform is organized: registration, app activation and package selection are described as steps, while later sections explain how levels, team matching and rank calculations are supposed to work. The speaker even introduces a section as an explanation of how rewards are calculated. That instructional structure supports reading the video as a walkthrough of stated rules, without treating its account as proof that the platform operates or pays as described.

citations.quote: What can we do here? There's a very simple step. All you have to do after your registration at BOTT is just turn on the BOTT app, select an investment package and activate it.
Here is how a reward calculation is done.
your team's left side business and right side business will be counted while matching it

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening quotes instructions and projected profits, but explaining an offer's steps is not by itself evidence that the steps were carried out or that the projections were realized. Likewise, describing first and second referral levels explains the stated structure; it does not show a particular viewer recruited anyone. The video can be evaluated as an explanation of claimed operations without certifying those claims.

citations.quote: Here is how a reward calculation is done.
Similarly, if he also subscribes to anyone, he will join you again on your second level.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is itself a pitch for participation. It says the only way to earn good money is to look at the named website, tells viewers to activate an investment package, and presents continuing profits as the result. An instructional format does not neutralize those direct investment and return claims.

citations.quote: The only way to earn good money via Boat trading is by looking at this website www. geniussarbitrageboat.net .
select an investment package and activate it. After that, you just keep getting profits through BOTT.

opening.argument: Judge, referral bonuses and tiered rewards can be read as the advertised terms of a promotional program, not proof of how it is funded. The speaker describes bonuses linked to referrals and a rank reward linked to a team-business threshold. The presentation also states withdrawal terms. None of those statements documents an actual deposit, a failed withdrawal or a payout funded by later participants. The precise funding and operation of this offer remain unverified in the supplied material.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening establishes that the speaker advertises investment returns and referral levels. It does not establish where bonus funds come from, whether anyone deposited money, or whether the stated returns were paid. The contact invitation is a route for inquiries, not evidence in itself of a credential request or completed transaction. Those missing facts limit what can be concluded about the program's actual mechanism.

citations.quote: For more details and information on this project, you can contact us by text or send us your email address, or by mail or email account.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern does not depend on proving a completed deposit or tracing payouts. The video asks viewers to invest in a package for stated daily bonuses, then describes compensation from a referred person's investment and further levels. That combination is materially different from an ordinary loyalty promotion, even though the record cannot establish whether the platform paid anyone.
